description.narrative:
The global confederation changes and new regional arrangement of Oxfam in Africa, Oxfam in Uganda continues to get in to terms withthe new ways of working since the coming in to effect of Oxfam in Africa from the 1st of April 2023. The country leadership continues to provide clarity to the country teams on the new ways of working, as the country office remains open to hosting a number roles in the Oxfam in Africa as part of diversified networks.
Oxfam in Uganda's Country Strategic Framework (2021-2030) reiterates Oxfam's commitment to fighting inequality working together with others, it introduces a new pillar which focuses on women's rights and gender justice. A new organogram was recently approved and was implemented in part during 2023/24 taking into consideration various internal changes in the confederation. According to Oxfam internal rating, Uganda continues to be not considered fragile and/or a riskcountry and yet the country hosts the largest number of refugees in Africa and continues to experience climate induced disasters and epidemics. Uganda also experiences proliferation of small arms and light weapons which cause instability and insecurity. This position continues to disadvantages Uganda in accessing internal resources. The fact that Uganda continues to operate as a full-fledged country program has implications on the scale and scope of our programming. While there has been an increase in CRA in the FY 2021/22, it still remains insufficient in supporting institutional costs required for effective programming. The country program has continued to receive unrestricted funding to complement programme financing from some partner affiliates. This support is anticipated to continue and possibly more partner affiliates will come on board. The Country Office also plans to increase its ability to raise costs recovery from restricted project funding.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
